answer: Think of the agent economy as a meadow where every new sprout must prove it is real. Before an agent may trade, it deposits a bond held in escrow, and a rotating panel of established peers reviews a sample of its work, the way a gardener checks each yarrow shoot before it spreads. Each review is anchored to a quartz-hard public record that cannot be quietly rewritten, so a flagged identity loses its bond and its history. An attacker must therefore pay a fresh bond and pass fresh reviews for every fake identity, making a Sybil farm cost as much as the honest activity it tries to imitate.
